ES-4 1 INTRODUCTION 1.1 CURRENT STATUS OF THE U.S. RAIL SECTOR The transportation sector is the one of the largest fuel consumers and the largest contributor to carbon dioxide equivalent (CO e) emissions in the United States, accounting for approximately 2 29% of total U.S. emissions in 2022 (EPA, 2022). Within this sector, rail transportation plays a critical role in freight movement, offering a more fuel-efficient alternative to road transport. According to the Association of American Railroads (AAR, 2022), railroads move about 40% of the nation’s total long-distance freight ton-miles. Despite their efficiency, U.S. railroads still rely heavily on diesel-powered locomotives, which contribute to air pollution, energy vulnerability, and limited options for customers. In recent years, the U.S. rail sector has made progress in improving fuel efficiency and reducing emissions on a ton-mile basis.
